newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Hang Seng leaps ahead in early morning trade.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng leaps ahead in early morning trade.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index leaped ahead at the opening bell, recovering more ground lost in the market's correction last Friday.
The Hang Seng Index advanced 164 points to 13,308 at the start of trading.But brokers expressed only limited optimism on the near-term outlook for the market.
Turnover was a healthy HK$800 million.
"We are moving in line with the Dow," said Peter Lai, associate director at OCBC Securities.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 82 points to 6,463.94 overnight, thus wiping out its Friday losses, in the belief that U.S. Federal Reserve would not put up interest rates in the near future.
On Friday, the Hang Seng Index dropped more than 600 points last Friday, before recovering some of that ground to end the day down 388 points.

"We are likely to stay within a broad trading range of 12,800 to 13,400," said Lai, adding that positive results from the government land auction to be held on Wednesday were already discounted within this range.
All sectors of the market advanced, led by the commercial and industrial sectors. But properties lagged the broad market.
The Hang Seng China Enterprises Index put on a strong 3.78 percent gain to 877.21, following in the wake of strong performances by foreign-investors-only B shares listed in Shenzhen and Shanghai.
Index heavyweight HSBC Holdings rose HK$1.50 to HK$161.50 and subsidiary Hang Seng Bank HK$1.75 to HK$92.00.
Cheung Kong put on HK$0.50 to HK67.25, but Sun Hung Kai was unchanged at HK$96.75.
Qingling Motors led the H share sector with an advance of HK$0.27 to HK$3.725.
Hang Seng Index futures trading was active in the first 30 minutes with the December contract rising to a high 13,380, a gain of 195 points, before falling to trend at the 13,350 level.
